title: Faithful projective plane transfer
question: Under explicit nonzero-ray, depth and invertibility conditions, which projective incidences and plane-induced image constraints survive a camera-frame change?
prior_work: Source has algebraic incidence, determinant and plane-motion lemmas; inspected theorem statements, not rebuilt in inventory.
obstacle: Vector identities do not alone establish a projective quotient camera pipeline or physical calibration; proposal overstates failure of epipolar geometry on planes.
crossover_seed: Use simulation relations from control to state the camera-model bridge.
cheap_test: Construct rational plane points and invertible H; check incidence and depth scaling, then test singular H and zero rays.

title: Homography pose ambiguity and cheirality
question: Given a calibrated plane-induced homography, which rigid pose and plane candidates satisfy reconstruction and positive-depth constraints, including degeneracies?
prior_work: Survey proposes analytical decomposition; existing Lean file only proves forward identities.
obstacle: Survey fixed eight-to-two multiplicity and novelty claims are not established; pure rotation, scale conventions and visible points can change ambiguity.
crossover_seed: Treat branches as finite certificates like SAT witnesses instead of assuming a solution count.
cheap_test: For identity, pure translation and generic rotation homographies, test candidate reconstruction and signed depths; report sets rather than fixed count.

title: Epipolar validity versus pose identifiability
question: When do calibrated two-view correspondences determine a rigid pose, and how do planar scenes or zero baseline affect identifiability without invalidating the epipolar identity?
prior_work: Lean source proves the epipolar equation from a depth-scaled relation even for arbitrary R; prose in proposal conflates validity with estimation ambiguity.
obstacle: Need separate SO(3), nonzero translation, nonzero rays and observability conditions; algebraic satisfaction is not unique reconstruction.
crossover_seed: Borrow observability rank tests and unobservable modes from control.
cheap_test: Build planar correspondences satisfying two distinct epipolar matrices, and a pure-rotation zero-E case; verify identity separately from rank.

title: Certifiable robust Wahba rotation
question: Can an outlier-corrupted rotation estimate carry a checkable lower-bound certificate matching its feasible objective under a stated noise/outlier model?
prior_work: QUASAR and robust rotation certification are listed and summarized in a local survey; no local replication found.
obstacle: Numerical PSD and claimed universal zero duality gap are insufficient; exactness depends on instance and assumptions.
crossover_seed: Reuse exact rational energy certificates from finite mathematics.
cheap_test: Construct a tiny rotation dataset with one controlled outlier and independently check primal residual and rational dual slack.

title: Robust point-cloud registration
question: Which translation/rotation/scale ambiguities and outlier patterns prevent a certifiable rigid point-cloud registration on small fixtures?
prior_work: TEASER is explicitly catalogued as a registration method; full source and algorithm not audited here.
obstacle: Must distinguish correspondences from correspondence search, bounded noise from adversarial data, and conditional certificate from guaranteed success.
crossover_seed: Use fault-isolation consistency sets and graph rigidity to predict ambiguous inlier subsets.
cheap_test: Create two congruent subcloud explanations and test whether a proposed certificate rejects ambiguity rather than selecting a convenient alignment.

title: Pose-graph synchronization certificates
question: Can a small inconsistent relative-pose graph be accompanied by an independently checked certificate of global optimum after gauge fixing?
prior_work: SE-Sync appears as a surveyed certifiable synchronization reference; no local pose-graph implementation inspected.
obstacle: Gauge freedom, disconnected graphs and relaxation tightness must be made explicit.
crossover_seed: Cycle invariants from graph theory and passivity-style residual budgets.
cheap_test: Use a three-node rotation cycle with one inconsistent edge and compare exact cycle residuals, feasible objective and a lower bound.

title: Complete minimal absolute-pose candidates
question: Can a P3P minimal solver produce all physically admissible camera poses for a three-point instance with a checkable real-root certificate?
prior_work: Survey names P3P in its minimal-solver transfer discussion; no P3P implementation or polynomial derivation checked.
obstacle: Numerical action-matrix eigenvalues are not automatically complete exact roots; singular and repeated-root cases need treatment.
crossover_seed: Transfer algebraic root isolation and certificate checking from exact mathematics.
cheap_test: Choose rational geometry, derive its range equations, isolate roots and reconstruct each pose; test collinear input rejection.

title: Minimal relative pose and degeneracy
question: Can a five-correspondence calibrated relative-pose solve distinguish isolated real solutions from degenerate solution families with a checkable certificate?
prior_work: Five-point relative pose is named in the survey; epipolar forward identity exists locally.
obstacle: Need actual elimination equations and saturation conditions; quotient-ring dimension and generic root count are not guarantees for every instance.
crossover_seed: Use rank stratification and control observability analysis before algebraic solving.
cheap_test: Compare a generic five-ray fixture with planar/pure-rotation fixtures; test rank and substitution residuals of all claimed candidates.

title: Point-line multiview reconstruction
question: For a selected small complete-visibility point-line configuration, can all consistent multiview reconstructions be enumerated and validated?
prior_work: PLMP and homotopy continuation are named as source-map leads; no configuration-level review evidenced.
obstacle: A named method is not a specified finite problem; choose one published configuration and verify path-completeness assumptions first.
crossover_seed: Translate incidence into hypergraph constraints and exploit automorphism reduction.
cheap_test: Select a triangle of point/line incidences in two or three views, count degrees of freedom, and exhibit a gauge or degeneracy witness before solver work.

title: Global bounded-reprojection feasibility
question: Under positive depth and fixed versus unknown rotations, which multiview maximum-reprojection-error subproblems admit convex feasibility certificates?
prior_work: Hartley/Kahl L-infinity optimization and rotation branch-and-bound are surveyed.
obstacle: Whole pose estimation is not made convex by naming an SOCP; rotation and denominator domains matter.
crossover_seed: Use reachable-set branch-and-bound and interval certificates from safety verification.
cheap_test: For two fixed cameras, test a triangulation error threshold using explicit cone inequalities; change rotation to show where fixed-camera convexity breaks.

title: Outlier admission in information filtering
question: Can a geometric outlier-rejection rule preserve a stated estimation-error bound when combined with an additive information update?
prior_work: Survey proposes combining pose rejection and information updates; source file supplies algebraic inverse identities only.
obstacle: Posterior covariance algebra does not bound actual error under biased or misclassified measurements; observation and noise assumptions are missing.
crossover_seed: Use robust set-membership observers and safety-margin erosion.
cheap_test: Scalar counterexample: very precise biased measurement decreases covariance while increasing actual error; then test bounded-error interval admission.

title: Planar camera calibration identifiability
question: Which planar checkerboard views provide enough independent constraints to recover camera intrinsics, and how can a calibration carry a rank/consistency check?
prior_work: Zhang calibration is cited as an application of homographies, not implemented or audited.
obstacle: Need calibration model, view diversity and noise assumptions; a homography proof does not prove intrinsic recovery.
crossover_seed: Experiment-design Gramians and persistent excitation from control.
cheap_test: Compare repeated fronto-parallel views to tilted synthetic views using the intrinsic-constraint matrix rank.

title: Task intent versus measurement ambiguity
question: What authoritative task information is necessary to distinguish a true small move from noisy observations of a hold without silently suppressing intended motion?
prior_work: Prior report gives identical-history impossibility examples and a later isolated authoritative-goal theorem under explicit premises.
obstacle: Intent remains a trusted input; identical numeric histories cannot reveal incompatible hidden tasks.
crossover_seed: Information-theoretic indistinguishability and typed command protocols.
cheap_test: Replay identical 1 mm packets under hold and move truths with disjoint 0.2 mm goal bands; demonstrate no packet-only universal success.

title: Reference continuity across native replanning
question: Can an execution adapter preserve the actual native trajectory jet across repeated replacements and retain all real jump contributions in its metrics?
prior_work: Native execution repair retains C++ trajectory state and reports finite reconstruction tests; tiny joins and jerk-side differences remain explicit.
obstacle: Finite sampled agreement is not continuous-runtime or firmware correctness; clock rounding and zero-duration metadata matter.
crossover_seed: Refinement relations from verified compilers applied to trajectory representations.
cheap_test: Use one superseded short native phase and compare both sides of q/v/a at execution joins under exact binary-origin conversion.

title: Atomic future commit under clock uncertainty
question: Can a candidate future trajectory be committed only while its history, task, frame and timing snapshot remains valid under bounded clock error?
prior_work: Addendum proposes versioned snapshot, future validation and atomic commit; current proof boundary assumes ideal common clock and atomic state.
obstacle: Ordering bounds do not establish atomic state binding or physical progress; real executor absent.
crossover_seed: Database serializability and optimistic concurrency control with interval time.
cheap_test: Enumerate interleavings of proposal, goal revision and commit; reject stale version even when time inequality passes.

title: Conditional scheduler progress
question: Under what feasible-task margin, candidate coverage, computation bounds and request-rate assumptions must the executor eventually accept a request?
prior_work: Addendum explicitly separates sound acceptance from progress and lists needed premises.
obstacle: An always-reject checker is sound but useless; a finite candidate search is not completeness.
crossover_seed: Fair scheduling and temporal-logic liveness certificates.
cheap_test: Small discrete scheduler model with a feasible execution slot; compare bounded exhaustive slot coverage to starvation under repeated supersession.

title: Bounded retained-history storage
question: Can the retained-event execution contract obtain a finite memory and checking-time bound while preserving all active and future commitments?
prior_work: Prior audit states finite but unbounded histories and roughly quadratic checking work; addendum notes pruning completed events does not bound active queues.
obstacle: Requires arrival-rate or admission assumptions; deleting future events changes the task.
crossover_seed: Network calculus arrival curves and queueing admission applied to proof certificate size.
cheap_test: Send arbitrarily dense accepted future events in one support window; derive counterexample to pruning-only bounded memory, then bound count under minimum spacing.

title: World-frame derivative transport
question: Can world-frame output constraints be preserved when body motion, frame/calibration updates and coupled robot kinematics transform an actuator reference?
prior_work: Addendum identifies frame derivative, calibration, singularity and coupled dynamics obligations; no proved multi-axis extension.
obstacle: Componentwise limits do not imply Cartesian bounds; rotating-frame terms and singularities can amplify error.
crossover_seed: Differential geometry covariant derivatives and robust Jacobian bounds.
cheap_test: Two-dimensional rotating base with constant body-frame vector: calculate nonzero world velocity/acceleration and expose an omitted transport term.

title: Minimal intervention on redundant arms
question: Can a robot avoid correcting task-irrelevant joint deviations while maintaining explicit task, obstacle and actuator constraints?
prior_work: Motor-control reading motivates minimal intervention; source explicitly says scalar model has no redundancy and cannot establish this extension.
obstacle: Null-space freedom can violate constraints and disappears near singularities; biological analogy is motivation only.
crossover_seed: Quotient-space goals, control allocation and task-space invariants.
cheap_test: Two-joint scalar task x=q1+q2: compare full joint correction with null-space motion while enforcing joint bounds; add a singular Jacobian case.

title: Energy benefit versus smoothness proxies
question: Does a smoother successful robot trajectory reduce a defined mechanical or electrical energy quantity once task, timing, payload and losses are matched?
prior_work: Prior addendum separates jerk integral, torque effort and joules; rest-to-rest frictionless net-work counterexample given.
obstacle: No electrical/mechanical energy measurement exists in scalar acceleration-command model; prior methods start revisions at different distances.
crossover_seed: Thermodynamic accounting and Pareto comparison with constraints.
cheap_test: Compare equal-duration rest-to-rest polynomials in an inertia-plus-viscous-loss model, reporting net work, positive work, loss and jerk separately.

title: Fair native industrial motion comparison
question: What common task and replacement semantics permit a fair comparison between an external execution contract and native buffered industrial interpolation?
prior_work: FANUC/Yaskawa documentation was read in bounded scope; no vendor hardware controller implemented or simulated.
obstacle: Stop-between-point, buffered target and incremental interfaces have distinct semantics; proprietary derivative objectives unknown.
crossover_seed: Experimental causal inference and interface trace equivalence.
cheap_test: Specify paired abstract buffered versus stop-at-each-point traces; show cycle-time advantage disappears or changes when interpolation ownership is matched.

title: Complete moving-goal admission contract
question: Can retained-history motion admission enforce velocity, acceleration, jerk and task deadline simultaneously during reversal, while competing with native online planning?
prior_work: Prior independently replayed scalar batch reports native 18/24 valid tasks versus FIR 6/24; jerk guard admits an acceleration excess and rejection leaves old goal active.
obstacle: Jerk-only correctness is insufficient; preserving old motion can cause large goal error. No universal planner replacement established.
crossover_seed: Multiobjective viability kernels and exact polynomial extrema rather than a single smoothness budget.
cheap_test: Reproduce ordinary-return exact acceleration 21/32 against 1/2 limit and far-reversal rejection; add full V/A/J feasibility check without changing history.

title: Moving-base gaze stabilization
question: Can a small execution layer maintain a world-frame optical output while a supporting robot moves and a slower visual task changes?
prior_work: Bird gaze and aerial optical-axis sources were read only at abstract/title level; addendum proposes separated stabilization/tracking loops and staged simulation.
obstacle: Need multirate delay, authority, signal and domain models; IMAX mechanism unverified and no universal tremor cause follows.
crossover_seed: Small-gain/passivity loop composition and vestibular feedforward as bounded engineering hypotheses.
cheap_test: Scalar base angle plus fast actuator and delayed outer visual loop; isolate coordinated feedforward versus inconsistent frame/loop state.

title: Franka model and total-torque transfer gap
question: What explicit coupled tracking and total-actuation contract could justify transferring scalar checked references to the recorded FR3 simulation or a specified physical Franka arm?
prior_work: Pinned seven-joint simulation found stock-actuator final failures and assisted final-window passes but 9.213 mm transient tracking error; assist lies outside force clamp.
obstacle: Exact hardware variant unknown; ideal bias assistance is not firmware, total torque is unbounded by retained actuator clamp, and sampled convergence is not proof.
crossover_seed: Assume-guarantee refinement with total resource budgets and task-space tubes.
cheap_test: From a recorded assisted state, sum position-actuator force and ideal bias force; test total bound and compare flange error against claimed scalar tube.
